hints: Fill the ordering one position at a time. For the first position, how many choices are there, and what do you need to remember so you don't reuse an element?
Backtracking with a used[] boolean array. At each position try every element not yet used, mark it, recurse, then unmark it.

1. Keep cur (the ordering so far) and used[].
  2. If cur has all n elements, save a copy.
  3. Otherwise loop over every index i; skip it if used[i].
  4. Mark used[i], add nums[i], recurse.
  5. Remove nums[i] and unmark used[i].

approaches.name: Optimal: backtracking with used[]
approaches.idea: Build each ordering position by position; there are n! orderings and each takes O(n) to copy, so this is as good as it gets.

explain: For [5,7,1]: put 5 first, then try 7 then 1 (giving 5,7,1) and 1 then 7 (giving 5,1,7). Then 7 first gives 7,5,1 and 7,1,5, and 1 first gives 1,5,7 and 1,7,5. That is 3! = 6 orderings. Unmarking after the recursive call is essential, otherwise an element stays 'used' for the next branch. A single element like [4] has just one ordering.
recognize: 'Return every ordering / arrangement of all elements' → permutation backtracking with a used[] array.
